C Verdict-led

The Two Gates

The catalogue opens as two painted doors. The Fire gate burns in the only full-color painting in the library — the crimson sun — so "the energy you need" is felt before it is read. The Earth gate sits beneath it, desaturated, quieter, smaller: the hierarchy itself is the verdict.

  • Color is the verdict. The catalyst gate is the sole colored artwork on the surface; friction is ink-quiet. Element pigment maps to meaning — never decoration.
  • Each gate carries the production headline verbatim ("The forge you borrow, never own" / "The ground that feeds your edge"), the canonical tag, and a depth tease naming the face inside (The General, The Alchemist).
  • The wheel is untouched, demoted to evidence beneath the gates; the remaining three energies collapse to compact rows.
  • Risk: two large art bands cost vertical space — the wheel falls below the fold on short phones.

D Meaning-led

The Scroll of Meaning

B-02's inscribed plate stays as the opening — then the page becomes a scripture scroll: five painted bands, one per energy, each teaching what the energy means first (the locked experiential line), stating the verdict second, and ending in a "read the deeper message" descent.

  • Meaning is the hook. Each band leads with the canonical experiential line — "the room is different before you speak" (Fire), "the verdict arrives before the conversation" (Metal). The user recognizes themselves before being told what to do about it.
  • The Fire band wears a catalyst ring and the only colored painting; friction bands are ink-quiet. Verdicts read in-line: the energy you need / the energy you don't.
  • Band order is presence-independent: catalyst first, friction second, then core and the rest — the prescription IS the sort order.
  • Longest surface of the three — deliberately. This variant bets that reading, not scanning, is the product.

The Compass

The wheel becomes an instrument, not a chart. A seal-red thread — the one permitted chop-red accent — runs from the Day Master seal to the catalyst node: your needle. A dashed ink line drags toward friction. Beneath, a single readout card answers all three questions for whichever energy is selected. This mockup is live — tap the nodes and chips.

  • One card, three answers. The readout stacks meaning (experiential line) → verdict (need/don't) → depth (the face inside + read arrow) for the selected energy. The whole catalogue fits one viewport — the locked no-scroll rule survives.
  • The thread teaches the wheel. Presence still sizes the disks, but the red thread makes "where should I look first" unmissable — it always lands on the catalyst, never the biggest disk.
  • The FEED / EASE chip index doubles as the role grouping from B-02, compressed to one line.
  • Risk: the readout shows one energy at a time — comparison across all five costs taps.

The second layer — faces as representations (confirm this lexicon)

After the user grasps Catalyst / Friction, the next layer of readability is what each energy says about them — personality, strengths, flaws — carried by the face inside the element and a single plain representation word. The words below follow the register you set in the earlier identity-card session (The Horizon = Enterprise); only Horizon's word is confirmed from that session — the other nine are derived from the locked keyword sets and need your sign-off (or the original list, if you have it, and I'll swap them in). The same lexicon feeds the Day Master identity card: each face a chart carries renders as face name · representation word · strengths/flaws keywords, so the second layer reads identically on both surfaces.

Studio recommendation

Test E against C. E honors the locked one-screen catalogue and makes the wheel — the product's signature — the answer machine itself; the red thread is the single most legible "what do I need" gesture of the three. C is the strongest pure first-impression and the best A/B against the tested confusion, but it spends the wheel. D is the richest reading surface and its band pattern should become the element reading pages' opening section regardless of which catalogue wins. All three keep the Catalyst / Friction vocabulary verbatim, the locked wheel geometry, production art, and production copy lines.
